title: A zero of the derivative of the absolute value
counterexample: $f(x) = |x|$ is not differentiable at $0$, and at every other point of $(-1, 1)$ its derivative is $1$ or $-1$; so no such $c$ exists.
claim: ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1, HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => |x|) 0 c

fragment: have hcont : ContinuousOn (fun x : ℝ => |x|) (Set.Icc (-1) 1) := continuous_abs.continuousOn

steps.text: Its values at the endpoints agree: $f(-1) = 1 = f(1)$.
fragment: have hend : |(-1 : ℝ)| = |(1 : ℝ)| := by norm_num

steps.text: By Rolle's theorem applied to $f$ on $[-1, 1]$, since $f(-1) = f(1)$, there is $c \in (-1, 1)$ with $f'(c) = 0$.
fragment: obtain ⟨c, hc, h0⟩ := exists_hasDerivAt_eq_zero (f' := fun x : ℝ => (SignType.sign x : ℝ)) (by norm_num) hcont hend (fun x _ => hasDerivAt_abs (by norm_num))
